args.question: What ImageNet top-5 classification error does the original ResNet paper report for its ILSVRC'15 ensemble? Identify the exact error, whether the result is on the validation or test set, whether it is single-crop, 10-crop, or multi-model ensemble, and the table/section where reported. Quote verbatim.

steps.purpose: Read the ResNet paper specifically for the ILSVRC'15 ensemble classification result and its evaluation setup.

result.answer:
Answer: ResNet’s ILSVRC’15 ensemble reports 3.57% top-5 error on the ImageNet test set; DenseNet-201 reports 6.34% single-crop and 5.54% 10-crop top-5 error on the ImageNet validation set. No—these are not like-for-like numbers: the ResNet figure is a six-model ensemble scored on the test set by the server, whereas the DenseNet-201 figures are an individual model’s validation-set results under single-crop/10-crop testing, so they cannot establish a head-to-head advantage.

ResNet: Table 5 lists ResNet (ILSVRC’15) at 3.57 and says the top-5 error is on the ImageNet test set and reported by the test server [S:43eecbafc161#53]. The text says six models of different depth were combined (only two 152-layer ones at submission) and this led to 3.57% top-5 error on the test set, winning ILSVRC 2015 [S:43eecbafc161#62]. The paper’s ImageNet setup uses 1.28 million training images and 50k validation images, plus a 100k test set whose result is reported by the test server [S:43eecbafc161#30].

DenseNet: Table 3 reports DenseNet-201 at 6.34 single-crop and 5.54 10-crop top-5 error, explicitly on the ImageNet validation set with single-crop/10-crop testing [S:20e50960076d#48]. Its ImageNet section says ILSVRC 2012 has 1.2 million training and 50,000 validation images, uses 224×224 single-crop or 10-crop testing, and reports classification errors on the validation set [S:20e50960076d#46]. The DenseNet paper says its comparison replaces the ResNet model with DenseNet-BC while keeping all experiment settings exactly the same as for ResNet, reporting single-crop and 10-crop validation errors [S:20e50960076d#66]; it also cautions that its hyperparameters were optimized for ResNets, not DenseNets [S:20e50960076d#67].

Thus the comparison is not apples-to-apples: ResNet’s 3.57% is an ensemble test-set result [S:43eecbafc161#53][S:43eecbafc161#62], while DenseNet-201’s 6.34%/5.54% are individual-model validation-set single/10-crop results [S:20e50960076d#48][S:20e50960076d#46]. The papers do not provide a shared protocol that would let these particular numbers establish a like-for-like advantage.

citations.text:
Comparisons with State-of-the-art Methods. In Table 4
we compare with the previous best single-model results.
Our baseline 34-layer ResNets have achieved very compet-
itive accuracy. Our 152-layer ResNet has a single-model
top-5 validation error of 4.49%. This single-model result
outperforms all previous ensemble results (Table 5). We
combine six models of different depth to form an ensemble
(only with two 152-layer ones at the time of submitting).
This leads to 3.57% top-5 error on the test set (Table 5).
This entry won the 1st place in ILSVRC 2015.

citations.title: arXiv:1512.03385v1  [cs.CV]  10 Dec 2015
citations.text:
4. Experiments
4.1. ImageNet Classiﬁcation
We evaluate our method on the ImageNet 2012 classiﬁ-
cation dataset [36] that consists of 1000 classes. The models
are trained on the 1.28 million training images, and evalu-
ated on the 50k validation images. We also obtain a ﬁnal
result on the 100k test images, reported by the test server.
We evaluate both top-1 and top-5 error rates.

citations.title: arXiv:1608.06993v5  [cs.CV]  28 Jan 2018
citations.text:
We simply replace the ResNet model with the DenseNet-
BC network, and keep all the experiment settings exactly
the same as those used for ResNet.
We report the single-crop and 10-crop validation errors
of DenseNets on ImageNet in Table 3.
Figure 3 shows
the single-crop top-1 validation errors of DenseNets and
ResNets as a function of the number of parameters (left) and
FLOPs (right). The results presented in the ﬁgure reveal that
DenseNets perform on par with the state-of-the-art ResNets,
whilst requiring signiﬁcantly fewer parameters and compu-
tation to achieve comparable performance. For example, a
DenseNet-201 with 20M parameters model yields similar
validation error as a 101-layer ResNet with more than 40M
parameters. Similar trends can be observed from the right
panel, which plots the validation error as a function of the
number of FLOPs: a DenseNet that requires as much com-
putat

ion as a ResNet-50 performs on par with a ResNet-101,
which requires twice as much computation.
It is worth noting that our experimental setup implies
that we use hyperparameter settings that are optimized for
ResNets but not for DenseNets. It is conceivable that more
extensive hyper-parameter searches may further improve
the performance of DenseNet on ImageNet.
